decisions.statement: A slot has the observer of the stream in flight or has nothing.
A slot with nothing in it is made here rather than written out by each caller.
A slot's end ends the stream that slot has.
A slot with no end is a slot nothing ends.
A wrapped end runs the end handed in on the first call.
A wrapped end called again runs the end handed in no further.
A wrapped end is one-shot for the life of that wrapper.
Two wrappers over the one end run that end twice.
A wrapped end is marked as run before the end handed in is called.
A caller putting a new observer in the slot ends the observer being replaced.
Nothing here ends a stream on its own.
Nothing here reads or writes the disk.
A slot takes an observer already terminated.
An end that throws is left marked as run.

definition: the one stream a connection has in flight, and the end that runs once
